guide.title: How to set up the spreadsheet & Service Account
guide.intro: Synchronization needs two things: the Spreadsheet ID of the Google Sheet you want to sync to, and a Service Account JSON from Google Cloud Console that has been shared on the spreadsheet as Editor. Follow these steps.

spreadsheetId.title: 1. Spreadsheet ID
spreadsheetId.step1: Open the Google Sheet you want to use (or create a new one at https://sheets.google.com).
spreadsheetId.step2: Look at the URL in your browser's address bar. It follows this pattern:
spreadsheetId.step3: Copy the ID portion — the long token between /d/ and /edit. In the example above it is: 1aBcDeFgHIjkLMNopQRstUvWxYz0123456789AbcDe.
spreadsheetId.step4: Paste it into the Spreadsheet ID field above.

serviceAccount.title: 2. Service Account (Google Cloud Console)
serviceAccount.step1: Open the Google Cloud Console at https://console.cloud.google.com/. Sign in with the same Google account (free, no credit card required).
serviceAccount.step2: Create a new project (or pick an existing one) from the project picker in the top-left.
serviceAccount.step3: Enable the Google Sheets API: open https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/sheets.googleapis.com and click Enable.
serviceAccount.step4: Open IAM & Admin → Service Accounts, click Create Service Account, give it a name (e.g. perpustakaan-sync), then Done.
serviceAccount.step5: After the Service Account is created, click it → Keys tab → Add Key → Create new key → JSON → Create. Your browser will download a JSON file.
serviceAccount.step6: Open the downloaded JSON in a text editor, copy the entire contents (from { to }), then paste into the Service Account JSON field above.
serviceAccount.step7: Click Save Service Account. The Service Account email will appear in the green box (its format is xxx@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com).

sharing.title: 3. Share the spreadsheet with the Service Account
sharing.intro: Unlike API keys, Service Accounts need Editor access on the spreadsheet to be able to write (push). For pull-only use, Viewer is enough. Steps:
sharing.step1: Open the spreadsheet → click the Share button (top-right).
sharing.step2: Paste the Service Account email from the green box above (xxx@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com).
sharing.step4: Uncheck "Notify people" — Service Accounts don't have an inbox.
sharing.step5: Click Share, then Done. The spreadsheet is now writable by your Service Account.

guide.devNote: Note: this PR covers push & pull for the Anggota table. Other tables (buku, eksemplar, peminjaman, …) will follow in subsequent releases.

sandbox.summary: Run the app against a separate sandbox database — handy for training without touching real data.
sandbox.activeDescription: The app is currently writing to a separate demo database. Automatic backups are skipped while demo mode is active.
sandbox.inactiveDescription: Turning on demo mode copies the live database to demo.db and reloads the app. Subsequent changes never touch the live data.
sandbox.bannerMessage: Demo mode active — changes don't touch the live data.
sandbox.confirmEnableDescription: The live database will be copied to demo.db. The app will reload and subsequent changes will never touch the live data.
sandbox.confirmDisableDescription: The demo database will be archived and the app returns to the live data after reload.
